game.name: Spelunky 2
game.short_description: Spelunky 2 builds upon the unique, randomized challenges that made the original a roguelike classic, offering a huge adventure designed to satisfy players old and new. Meet the next generation of explorers as they find themselves on the Moon, searching for treasure and missing family.

commentary.label: Tier list Part 1 (2023)
commentary.summary: Spelunky 2 is the 2020 sequel to the classic Spelunky, a brutal, secret-filled platformer roguelike. PepperHead admits it is not his preferred play style and he has only about five hours in it, so he treats this as a partial review. He found it more fun and more readable than the original, with great art and VFX, but still very punishing later on. He places it in B tier with the note that he may bump it up once he plays more.
praise: Traps and overall readability feel easier and clearer than the first game
Even more secrets and things to find than the original
He respects the amount of work put in and understands why many would rank it S tier
criticism: Still super brutal; later in a run things explode and you die quickly
Not his kind of play style, limiting how much he enjoys it
He has limited playtime, so his verdict is provisional
unique_points: A huge number of secrets to discover, many found online
Sequel improves visual clarity of what is happening on screen
Strong VFX that contribute to feel
commentary.quote: I'm gonna put it as a solid beat here that I might bump up
comparisons: Rogue Legacy (as a similar old-game-gets-sequel case)
design_criteria: Difficulty: brutal, with late-run spikes that kill quickly
Readability: clearer visuals make traps and hazards easier to parse
Art and VFX: praised as excellent
Personal play-style fit: affects his enjoyment
Early vs late run pacing: gentle early, explosive late
commentary.rerank_note: He explicitly says the B placement is provisional and he might bump it up in the future after more playtime.

community.one_liner: Derek Yu's 2D procedurally generated platformer-roguelike sequel in which Ana Spelunky, daughter of the original hero, descends through a much larger, more interconnected set of caves on the Moon, with one-life runs, physics-driven chaos and optional 4-player co-op or arena play.
community.consensus_summary: Spelunky 2 is received as a superb, more-of-the-same-but-bigger sequel: critics gave it near-universal acclaim (PC Metacritic 91, IGN 10/10) and Steam players rate it Very Positive (about 93% of roughly 22k reviews). Praise centres on its deep systems, secrets, mounts, branching paths and hilarious emergent deaths. The recurring caveats are brutal difficulty with hidden one-hit-kill hazards, a no-save/no-checkpoint structure that turns the true ending (Cosmic Ocean) into a multi-hour endurance test, and, in recent Steam reviews, long-running online multiplayer/crossplay bugs. Some long-time fans feel it is slightly less tightly balanced than Spelunky HD. It is a finished, shipped game (PC/PS4 2020, Switch 2021, Xbox 2022, PS5 2025) rather than early access, though developer updates appear to have been sparse after the initial patches.
best_things: Systems-driven chaos: liquids, fire, explosives, thrown items and enemy interactions create funny, memorable emergent stories (players describe deaths as punchlines)
Huge, dense secret and unlock content with branching paths (Jungle/Volcana, Tide Pool/Temple), alternate routes, and shortcuts that reward exploration
Mounts (turkeys, rock dogs, axolotls, qilins) and new environments add real tactical variety while keeping the classic feel
Strong mastery loop: reviewers and players describe progress as learning to read threats, with winning a run being unusually satisfying
Polished art, animation and soundtrack, more expressive visuals than the original, plus a coherent world with NPCs and a family-themed story
Excellent couch and online co-op for up to four players, plus a customizable arena/deathmatch mode with 40 maps and bots, daily challenges and seeded runs
Enormous replay value; many Steam reviewers have 100 to 1000+ hours and call it a near-perfect or desert-island game
Quality-of-life improvements over the first game (e.g. more consistent shopkeeper balance, expanded exploration) that some players think make it more approachable
Best with friends: reviewers repeatedly say the chaos and deaths are funniest in co-op, and a few call it a calming, even cozy, game once you learn its rules
worst_things: Many instant-death or combo-death situations, including hidden hazards such as bear traps concealed by terrain, which critics (e.g. Destructoid) called frustrating and players call cheap or trolling

Online multiplayer problems widely reported on Steam: stuck on the loading screen, inability to join, crossplay-related breakage, and a bug requiring workaround input to load the next area; some reviewers say it has been broken for months or over a year
Perceived lack of developer communication/support after launch; Steam complaints mention no word from the developers for a long stretch
The Dwelling, Jungle and Volcana are called disproportionately hard for early worlds by some veterans, and certain levels feel specially designed to ruin a run
Some dedicated players feel the added mechanics (and the 'Sunken City'/Cosmic Ocean path requirements) dilute the tight risk-reward balance of Spelunky HD
Movement/controls friction: no dedicated pickup/drop/throw/climb buttons, leading to accidental climbs or item handling mistakes that kill the run
Short-range whip and thrown-item ricochet feel punishing to newcomers, who complain about taking damage just to hit a stationary enemy
Gameplay randomness (seed quality, needing specific items to spawn for shortcut unlocks) is cited as unfair by players who wrote negative reviews
improvements: Fix online co-op stability and crossplay bugs, and communicate about fixes on the Steam forums

Offer optional accessibility or difficulty options (e.g. extra health, easier modes, checkpoints/continues); one reviewer called their absence sadistic, though the developers deliberately preserve the no-continue design
Reduce reliance on concealed or unreadable hazards so deaths feel more telegraphed and learnable
Add dedicated buttons or rebind options for pick up/drop/throw/climb to reduce accidental actions
Smooth the early-game difficulty ramp (Dwelling and Jungle in particular) and make unlock requirements less dependent on random spawns
More post-launch communication and updates; reviewers complain of over a year of silence while plush merchandise was announced
unique_things: Every level is a hand-tuned procedural layout built from templates, so runs feel random but readable and fair at a systems level; the series is the reference for this style
Permadeath with literally no meta-progression in power: only shortcuts, unlocks and knowledge carry over, so skill is the main upgrade
Shared physics and item interactions where almost anything can kill you, including your own thrown items, enabling speedrun and trick strategies
Branching world structure with hidden areas, alternate paths and a secret true ending (Cosmic Ocean) requiring a long perfect run
Integrated multiplayer modes: 4-player couch and online co-op over the same campaign, and a full arena deathmatch mode with map variety
Distinct personalities for shopkeepers, NPC family members and the ghost mechanic that punishes slow play
tedious_or_disliked: Cosmic Ocean: a many-hour endurance sequence with no saves that many call the main grind; Steam reviewers joke about not being able to spare four hours and about few reaching it
Starting over from 1-1 after a sudden death, which newcomers and some critics (Gameblog.fr at 60/100) find unpedagogical and demoralizing
Repeated tedious retries to unlock shortcuts and characters, with rewards like a victory screen and a new character considered underwhelming by some
Status effects such as poison and curse described as run-ending annoyances
Fighting the interface and inputs (accidentally climbing or not being able to drop items) rather than the game
Bug-related restarts in online mode, such as getting stuck on the 'walls are shifting' screen
divisive_points: Difficulty and fairness: fans call it a masterclass, others call it a troll game; critics at Destructoid and GameSpot (8/10) noted excess one-hit-kill traps while IGN scored it 10/10
Versus Spelunky HD: some find 2 the better, more expansive game, while others think HD's risk-reward balance was tighter and that 2 is merely 'more Spelunky' with added complexity
Randomness vs skill: some players love the unpredictability, others argue too many deaths come from unfair spawns rather than player error
No-continue philosophy: praised as the source of the game's tension and reward, criticised as disrespectful of player time and a barrier that steers casuals away
community.reception_notes: Launched on PS4 (Sept 15, 2020) and PC (Sept 29, 2020) to universal acclaim and a Best Indie nomination at The Game Awards 2020; later ports came to Switch (Aug 2021), Xbox One/Series (Jan 2022) and PS5 (Mar 2025). Launch reception was about difficulty and refinement; the current Steam conversation (recent negatives) is dominated by online co-op and crossplay breakage, with reviewers saying a crossplay update made friend sessions unreliable and that developer communication is scarce. Gameblog.fr (60/100) was the notable critical outlier on pedagogy and progression. Revenue figures are third-party estimates only; no official sales numbers were found. OpenCritic score could not be retrieved: the web search budget was exhausted and the guessed OpenCritic URLs returned other games, so it is left null. Metacritic critic score depends on platform (PC 91, main page 87 (41 reviews), Switch 92); PC is used here to match the Steam listing, and the 8.0 user score came from the main (PS4) page.
